### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-openapi`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **12** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cf7f389fc9d5f8b1b2b78474b4058327ed5327f1` — the merge of head `615683feb3c9472259fdcc1dfefc73028d1b9d46` into base `e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cf7f389fc9d5f8b1b2b78474b4058327ed5327f1 && git checkout cf7f389fc9d5f8b1b2b78474b4058327ed5327f1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b 615683feb3c9472259fdcc1dfefc73028d1b9d46 && git checkout -B drift-repro e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b && git merge --no-ff 615683feb3c9472259fdcc1dfefc73028d1b9d46

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e1dde1a5c15566bcc24d6c641b53d8282fcf655b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7c7eed0d44f88f0df94655ba2a050864b2dac91d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-input-schema.test.ts, .changeset/27995-connector-action-input-schema.md + packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts (buildInputSchema, the per-action handler, interpolatePath, stringifyValues, buildUrl, applyAuth), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-slack/src/slack-connector.ts, packages/connectors/connector-rest/src/rest-connector.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/value-slot-map.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (NodeExecutionResult, getConnectorDescriptors, resolveConnectorActionEffect, the FLOW_INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID retry short-circuit), packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts (ConnectorActionSchema.inputSchema), skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-automation/references/integration-recipes.md, content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx, card #27968

Reviewed at 2026-10-30T10:06Z, adversarially, on: the net diff origin/main...pr28035 (base f29633407c7436675f0594165cf67519cb8f6598, 3 files, +378/-0), card #27995 (body; triage 6517799549; claim 6518217530 and amendment 6518274130; os-dev-report 6519820229), the PR body, file list and comments (Contract-review-claim 6519856849), and the head's check-runs. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Premise holds.** On main the executor hands the evaluated `connectorConfig.input` to the handler with no comparison against the action's `inputSchema`; the openapi handler then interpolates a missing path value as the literal placeholder (interpolatePath leaves `{petId}` when the value is null or undefined), which is the card's measured `/pets/%7BpetId%7D`.
- **Placement.** The check runs after `resolveValueSlotMap` (so envelopes are judged on their evaluated value — pinned) and before `handler()`; the root is always a plain object (`resolveValueSlotMap` returns `{}` for an absent map); on a refusal the handler is never called (pinned by the `sent` recorder in every refusal test). The schema is read from `getConnectorDescriptors()`, whose `inputSchema: a.inputSchema` is the stored def's value unchanged, so what is enforced is what `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors` shows.
- **Error contract: right code, right class, no leak.** `VALIDATION_ERROR` is the first member of `StandardErrorCode` (ADR-0112 D2, the 400 bucket; the pull door in connector-pull.ts answers its own input faults with the same code), carried on `NodeExecutionResult.code` onto `$error.code` (pinned through a `fault` edge). `errorClass` is left at its `runtime` default, so a `fault` edge or `try_catch` routes it — correct, since the input can come from run data; a `guard` refusal would be unroutable. The message names the node, `connectorId.actionId`, each violation by dotted path with the declared type beside the kind received, caps at five then a count, states nothing was sent, and prescribes `connectorConfig.input` plus the connectors route (served by dispatcher-plugin.ts; route-ledger row `GET /automation/connectors`). Only schema keys, array indices and JSON kinds appear: no input value leaks. Consistent with the executor's other `connector_action 'id':` refusals.
- **The subset is safe on the producers' real shapes** for everything it declines to judge: mcp passes `tools/list` schemas through verbatim and the walker skips `$ref`/`$defs`, `anyOf`/`oneOf`/`allOf`, `enum`, `format`, bounds, `additionalProperties`, boolean sub-schemas and tuple `items`, reading `required` only off the object it is on (no parent misread); 3.1 type lists and 3.0 `nullable` both admit null; `integer` is a whole number (bigint included); a `Date`/`Map` is unjudged; slack's literals and rest's `request` (no `required`, untyped `body`) behave as before. Array-of-object `required` is reached through `items`. Arrays and body wrapped under a key are judged where they sit.
- **False refusals found — the openapi provider's `path`/`query`/`header` sections are string-serialized and null-dropping (stringifyValues drops null/undefined and applies String(v); buildUrl drops null; interpolatePath applies String(value)), and the check judges them as JSON:**
  1. **MUST-FIX — `null` on an OPTIONAL property is refused** (`'query.tag' must be string, got null`) although the provider drops it and the wire equals omission, which the schema permits. A CEL envelope over an empty record field (`{"tag": rec.tag}`) yields exactly this, and such a call succeeded before this head. Treat null/undefined on a property that is not in `required` as absent; keep judging null on a REQUIRED property (interpolatePath would send the literal placeholder — the card's bug), and keep `nullable`/type-list null as is.
  2. **MUST-FIX (cited producer) — buildInputSchema demands parameters the connector's `auth` supplies.** An `Authorization` or api-key header, or an api-key query `paramName`, declared as a required parameter in the document lands in that section's `required`, the section becomes root-required, and `input: {}` is refused with `missing required 'header'` (or `'query'`). OAS 3.0.3 §4.7.12.1 says `Accept`/`Content-Type`/`Authorization` header parameters SHALL be ignored; applyAuth overwrites them after the input merge anyway, so the demanded value could never take effect; the only way through is to write the credential into `connectorConfig.input`, which the platform forbids. Harmless while the schema was advisory; this narrowing makes every call on such an action fail. Fix at the producer — `buildInputSchema(op, auth)` in openapi-connector.ts drops the three reserved header names and the header/param `auth` supplies (the `auth` is in scope in createOpenApiConnector). That is a connector-openapi edit: the claim's file surface said stop on breach and report, and the report named the shape (inventory item 1) without naming the breach. The seat widens the surface for it.
  3. **SHOULD-FIX — the string spelling of an `integer`/`number`/`boolean` parameter in those sections** (`path.petId: '7'`, `query.limit: '10'`) is refused although the provider sends String(value) and the wire is byte-identical to the number. A text field holding a vendor id feeding an integer path parameter is routine; the changeset declares this refusal as intended. Either coerce in the string-serialized sections (what OpenAPI request validators do) or make the CEL cast (`int()`) the prescription in the error text and the changeset's Fix line. Strict judging stays right for `body` and for mcp arguments, which travel as JSON.
- **False passes: none found.** `getPet {}` and `{ path: {} }` refuse; the `path` section is root-required whenever present; nested `required` is reached through `properties` and `items`; a `required` name absent from `properties` is still judged.
- **Inventory and battery versus the real schemas.** The in-repo flows pass literal `{}` or strings to string parameters; the showcase openapi `getHealth` has no `inputSchema` and the mcp fixture requires only `text`. Neither the inventory nor the battery at this head exercises null on an optional parameter, a numeric string, or an auth-declared parameter — the inventory is honest about what exists in-repo and blind to 1–3 above.
- **Other doors.** connector-pull.ts dispatches the same handlers (`handler(input, …)` built from `connectorSource.input` plus the watermark query) without this check — the same defect through the pull door, outside this card's title; it is a finding to file, not a fix here. No REST route and no MCP-server tool invokes a connector action directly; AI tools reach connectors through flows, so they are covered.
- **#27968 untouched.** No registration-time judging was added; constants stay on that card's ledger path as triage ruled.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/service-automation` **patch — correct.** `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: registration and `objectstack validate` accept the same authorable text as before (the refusal is at dispatch; a registration-door narrowing would be `narrowed`, and that is #27968), so the level follows the kind, and the `!` title, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none` and the single ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` ride on patch (Post-Task Checklist step 3; a non-protocol breaking change ships patch and keeps banner and disposition). Both declaration lines appear in the PR body and the changeset body; the changeset carries FROM, TO, who sees it and the Fix. The `fixed` group versions the package with the rest. `Check Changeset` and the lint gates carrying the ADR-0087 and changeset checks are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviations, accepted:** PR-body attribution through the thread harness (the seat may patch the body to the seat form); the subset checker inline in connector-nodes.ts rather than a new module (file surface).
- **Open questions:** none declared; the three findings in ① are the ones this review owes back.
- **Out-of-scope findings:** the dev's one (descriptor list rebuilt per dispatch; carrier none) — accepted; a `resolveConnectorActionInputSchema` beside `resolveConnectorActionEffect` reading the stored def is the right home. **Missing:** the pull-door sibling named in ① — PD #10 asks for every call site; the seat files it.
- **Retry.** `runtime` makes the refusal routable, but under `errorHandling.strategy: 'retry'` a literal-only input re-derives a certainty 1+maxRetries times — the maintainer ruled the sibling `FLOW_INPUT_SCHEMA_INVALID` non-retryable for exactly that reason. Constants are #27968's path by triage; carry the note there, no change here.
- **`Skills-docs: none` — SHOULD-FIX.** skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md line 88 and references/integration-recipes.md line 18 teach that `connectorConfig.input` "is sent as written"; this head falsifies it (an incomplete or mistyped input is not sent), and content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx's failure-modes table has no row for the new refusal. Rewrite the line to `follow-up owed — FILES`; the seat files the card and rewrites it to `#N` before ACCEPT.
- **Dogfood battery at the final head is on record** in report 6519820229 (2026-10-30T09:48Z) and in the PR body: 357 files passed / 3 skipped, 2875 tests passed / 20 skipped, os-verify-lock command-exit 0.
- **Check-runs on the head, read at 2026-10-30T10:06Z:** 52 runs, all completed — 37 `success`, 15 `skipped` (the UI and opt-in lanes, paths-filtered), 0 failed, 0 in progress. Green among them: Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, Plan Test Core shards and Test Core 1–8, Type Check · workspace / source gates / debt ledger / consumer gates, every Lint lane, Check Changeset, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Live E2E UI. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this review adds none.

### ④ Design judgment

- **connector-nodes.ts — MUST-FIX ①1; SHOULD-FIX ①3; SHOULD-FIX** read the schema from the stored def (as `resolveConnectorActionEffect` does) instead of rebuilding the descriptor list per dispatch; nit: when a required object section is absent, also name its own required children (`path.petId`) so the first refusal already carries the parameter. The hand-written subset over a shared validator is sound: ajv is objectql-private (a devDependency here), compiles `$ref` eagerly, rejects an unknown `$schema`, and does not know `nullable`, so it would mis-refuse the very shapes mcp and openapi emit; a dependency change is outside the claim. The no-new-dependency reasoning holds.
- **connector-input-schema.test.ts — SHOULD-FIX.** The three schemas are hand-copied replicas, and the real-door probe (LiteKernel + ConnectorOpenApiPlugin) is uncommitted, so the `getPet {}` false pass is pinned against a replica, not against `buildInputSchema`'s output. Pin it in connector-openapi's own suite (openapi-provider.test.ts already boots `AutomationEngine`) through `createOpenApiConnector`, and add preservation pins for null-on-optional and an auth-declared parameter once ①1–2 land. 11 tests / 7 red before / 7-leg ablation: meaningful — the single `&& false` ablation reds exactly the seven refusal pins and leaves the four preservation pins green, as it should.
- **.changeset/27995-connector-action-input-schema.md — SHOULD-FIX** after ①1–3: re-state the "Who sees it" example (the `'7'` case) and the Fix line (cast or coercion); declarations, marker and migration prose are otherwise complete.
- **openapi-connector.ts (cited) — MUST-FIX ①2.**
- **mcp-connector.ts, slack-connector.ts, rest-connector.ts, value-slot-map.ts, engine.ts, connector.zod.ts (cited) — hold** against the hunks' claims.
- **connector-pull.ts (cited) — file** the sibling.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgUCizoYWQVJWjhdR6F`

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `615683feb3c9472259fdcc1dfefc73028d1b9d46`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/27995-connector-action-input-schema.md, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/input-schema-dispatch.test.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-connector.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-input-schema.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/connector-nodes.ts + packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/openapi-provider.ts, packages/connectors/connector-openapi/src/connector-openapi-plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts (ConnectorAPIKeySchema, RestAuth's source union), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (getConnectorDescriptors, celScope), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/value-slot-map.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts (GET /connectors), packages/formula/src/cel-engine.test.ts and cel-error-classification.test.ts (the dialect's int/double/bool), packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts (#28040), connector-nodes.ts as #28037 left it on main

Delta review at 2026-10-30T11:36Z, adversarially, of head 615683fe against the FAIL record 6520142501 (2026-10-30T10:07Z) on 7c7eed0d. Read: the net diff origin/main...pr28035 (base now 847e4248, 5 files, +602/-2) against the old net diff (3 files, +378/-0); the two non-merge commits since 7c7eed0d (b2149dc0, 67857097); claim amendment 2 6520164540 (2026-10-30T10:08Z); os-dev-report 6521455883 (2026-10-30T11:22Z); the PR body, file list and comments (claim 6521477850 on this head); the head's check-runs. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run; the one merge below is a server-free `git merge-tree` read. Every judgment of 6520142501 not named here stands unchanged at this head: premise, placement, error contract, the unjudged subset's safety on the three producers' shapes, no false passes, #27968 untouched, the pull-door sibling, the retry note.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The delta is the two patch commits and nothing else.** `git log --no-merges origin/main..head` lists a9f9f280, c75e9aa9 (the old head's content) plus b2149dc0 (connector-nodes.ts, its test, the changeset) and 67857097 (openapi-connector.ts, the new openapi test, the changeset); neither touches a path outside the five. The merge 615683fe equals its second parent e1dde1a5 (an ancestor of origin/main) outside the five files and its first parent 67857097 on them, so the raw 75-file old-to-new diff is main's motion, not the PR's. Main has since moved again: #28037 (b59bf60c) edited connector-nodes.ts after e1dde1a5. GitHub reports the PR mergeable and clean; a read-only `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main head` produces one file in which the #28016 held-instance refusal sits before handler resolution, input evaluation and this check, so the two refusals compose (a held instance refuses before its input is judged) and the queue leg has nothing to resolve by hand.
- **Must-fix ①1, null on an optional property — resolved, at every level.** `collectInputSchemaViolations` now builds `required` as a set per object and, in the property loop, `continue`s on `record[key] === null` when the key is not in it; the required loop still counts a missing key or `undefined` as missing. The recursion runs the same two loops at each object it reaches, so the rule holds for the root, each section, a nested object and an object inside `items` alike. `undefined` behaves as absent everywhere (skipped in the property loop, missing in the required loop). `null` on a REQUIRED property is still judged: it falls through to the type test and reads `'path.petId' must be integer, got null`, with no cast hint (pinned). `nullable: true` and a type list holding `null` admit null as before. A `null` array ITEM is not a property and is still judged against `items` (refused unless nullable), which is right for a JSON body and for mcp arguments. Pinned: service-automation 14 tests (3 new: null-required refused; null-optional dispatches, on a non-nullable boolean; the int() cast dispatches), and the dev's ablation of the single `continue` reds exactly the null-optional pin (1 failed / 13 passed, blob restored); and in connector-openapi test 2, on `buildInputSchema`'s real output over `tag: { type: string }` (not nullable), the call is sent and the recorded URL carries no `tag`.
- **Must-fix ①2, `buildInputSchema(op, auth)` — resolved, and it mirrors `applyAuth` branch for branch.** A header parameter whose lower-cased name is `accept`, `content-type` or `authorization` is dropped (OAS 3.0.3 §4.7.12.1). The api-key header is dropped when `auth.type === 'api-key' && !auth.paramName`, compared lower-cased against `headerName ?? 'X-API-Key'`, which is exactly `applyAuth`'s else-arm and the spec default in `ConnectorAPIKeySchema`; the api-key query parameter is dropped by exact name when `paramName` is set, which is `applyAuth`'s first arm (query names are case-sensitive, so exact is right). `bearer` and `basic` set only `Authorization`, covered by the ignored set; `none` sets nothing; `oauth2` is outside `RestAuth` (the open-source subset) so `applyAuth` has no arm for it and nothing is supplied or dropped, consistent; `ConnectorAPIKeySchema` has no cookie location (only `headerName`/`paramName`), and a document's `in: cookie` parameter was already skipped. A section left with no properties is not emitted and so is not root-required (pinned 3a: the schema has no `header` key); a section left with only optional parameters loses `sec.required` and so its root-required entry. Call sites: `git grep buildInputSchema` at this head finds one, line 217 of `createOpenApiConnector`, where `auth` is already `config.auth ?? { type: 'none' }`; the declarative provider (openapi-provider.ts) passes `ctx.auth` as `RestAuth` into that same generator, so a declaratively registered connector gets the same schema. What is published: the def's `inputSchema` reaches designers only through `registerConnector` → `getConnectorDescriptors()` (engine.ts, `inputSchema: a.inputSchema`, unchanged) → `GET /api/v1/automation/connectors`; no MCP tool and no AI catalog reads a connector action's inputSchema (grep across packages), so the one published shape and the one enforced shape are the same object, pinned by 3a/3b reading the descriptor. Side effects: the handler, `interpolatePath`, `stringifyValues`, `buildUrl` and `applyAuth` are untouched; an input that still writes `header.Accept` or a non-credential header passes (additionalProperties is unjudged) and reaches the wire as before, `Authorization` then overwritten by `applyAuth` as before; `Accept` is not set by the transport, so only its advertisement is lost. Observation, acceptance-note grade: a programmatic `defaultHeaders` entry can also supply a document-required header and the schema still demands it; unlike the auth case the input's value takes effect (input headers override defaults), the declarative provider passes no `defaultHeaders`, and nothing in-repo passes one to this generator, so it is not a false refusal of the kind ①2 named.
- **Should-fix ①3, no coercion, cast prescription — accepted as implemented, and the text is accurate.** Text is never converted; the refusal appends `cast it in a CEL envelope with int(), double() or bool()` only when a string met a declared integer, number or boolean (`textForScalar`), so a null-on-required or wrong-object refusal carries no misleading hint (pinned). The dialect is right: value envelopes go through `evaluateValueEnvelope` to the formula package's CEL engine (`@marcbachmann/cel-js`), whose `int("3")`, `double("3.5")` and `bool("true")` are pinned as stdlib in packages/formula/src/cel-engine.test.ts, with their conversion errors classified in cel-error-classification.test.ts. The changeset's Fix example `int(record.vendor_id)` names a real scope handle (`record` is the trigger record's alias of `$record` in `celScope`). The TO bullet ("Text is never converted"), the Who-sees-it line (the `"7"` case, "the error then says to cast it") and the Fix line (the envelope with `int()`, `double()`, `bool()`) agree with each other and with the code. The nit landed too: a missing required section names its required children (`missing required 'path' (with 'path.petId')`), pinned in both suites.
- **New tests.** `input-schema-dispatch.test.ts` boots LiteKernel + AutomationServicePlugin + ConnectorOpenApiPlugin with a recording `fetchImpl` and reads the schema off the live descriptor, so every pin is on `buildInputSchema`'s real output at the real door, which is what 6520142501 asked for. The fixture declares `X-Api-Key` and `Authorization` as required headers and `api_key` as a required query parameter, so with openapi-connector.ts at the previous commit every call without a `header` section was refused for `missing required 'header'`: tests 2, 3a and 3b red, test 1 green because the executor's refusal already stood from a9f9f280 and nothing in the fixture can admit `{}`.
